Hi Marissa / Ben —

Quick escalation request for Lumina Health (DL-47281). They’re asking for a 3-year commitment with the following non-standard terms:
- Fixed per-token price for 36 months (price lock) with an uplift cap of max +5% annually
- Renewal protection: automatic renewal at same tier unless Lumina gives 90 days notice; no forced market repricing in renewal year
- Add-on: extended support window and dedicated priority queue during business hours

Why this matters: Lumina is a strategic healthcare prospect (payer + provider integrations) — if we win this commit we expect ~ $3.1M ARR run-rate over the 3-year term with upsell potential to Dedicated. Procurement pushed hard on price stability and renewal protection; they flagged that if we can’t match this language they will pause the SOW.

Request: I’m asking Deal Desk + Exec sign-off to approve the price lock + uplift cap structure with the following recommended guardrails:
- Max uplift cap: 5% per year
- Redwood reserves right to convert to list pricing for materially increased unit-costs (e.g., hardware cost delta >20%) with 60 days notice
- Approval contingent on updated SOW and legal review (I’ve attached the latest SOW and price matrix)

Attachments: Lumina_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_price_matrix.xlsx

Next step: Marissa / Ben, can you put this into the approval queue and route to Laura for exec approval? If you want me to join the call with Lumina procurement, I’m available Mon/Tue.

Thanks —

Thanks Jonas — I’ve pulled the numbers and kicked this into Deal Desk triage. A few clarifying notes before we route to execs:

1) ARR / margin impact: the redwood_price_matrix.xlsx shows ~ $3.1M revenue over 3 years at the proposed locked rate, gross margin impact of ~ 18% vs standard list. We need exec sign-off for anything where expected margin drop > 12%.
2) Risk: Procurement also asked for a clause to prevent us from increasing price due to model upgrades. We should avoid an absolute bar on model substitution; suggest language that allows us to change model variants if functionally equivalent with notice.
3) Renewal protection: procurement wants "no re-pricing at renewal"; legal prefers a time-boxed protection (one renewal cycle). Suggest we offer protection for the first renewal only, subject to business review.

I’m preparing a one-pager for Laura with the financials and suggested conditional language. Can you confirm whether Lumina will accept a model-substitution carve-out (notify + equivalent performance guarantee) and whether they expect SSO/KMS additions (this affects infra cost)?

Laura — looping you in with a short summary and the Deal Desk one-pager (see inline).

Summary: Lumina procurement is ready to sign a 3-year SOW if we provide: a per-token price lock for 36 months, max uplift cap 5% annually, and renewal protection (they asked for indefinite protection; we recommend 1 renewal cycle protection). The economics: ~$3.1M revenue over 3 years at proposed rates; expected margin delta vs list ~18%.

Proposed conditions for Exec sign-off:
- Approve price lock + 5% uplift cap for 36 months
- Renewal protection limited to the first renewal (one additional 12-month term)
- Model substitution allowed if functionally equivalent with 30 days notice and opportunity to validate outputs against baseline prompts
- Redwood may exit price lock with 60 days notice if external hardware costs rise >20%

Why we recommend this: protects revenue and relationship while keeping operational flexibility. Lumina is asking for a market-leading package; losing this would likely push them to a competitor with weaker privacy controls.

If approved, I will instruct Legal to finalize the updated SOW and the Deal Desk will prepare an approval form for signature.

Thanks team — I reviewed the ask and the Deal Desk analysis. I approve the requested commercial structure with the following explicit conditions (please ensure these are redlined into the SOW and exec approval form before countersignature):

1) Price lock for 36 months at the agreed per-token rate; uplift capped at 5% per year (not compounding).
2) Renewal protection applies to one renewal only (the first renewal term). After that, standard market repricing applies.
3) Model substitution carve-out: Redwood may substitute to a functionally equivalent model variant with 30 days notice; we will provide a short evaluation report demonstrating parity on Lumina's required prompt-suite.
4) We reserve a unilateral exit right with 60 days notice if external infrastructure costs increase >20% (applies only to hardware-driven cost increases).
5) Legal must add a data-handling annex addressing PHI routing and KMS controls; deal is conditional on acceptance of that annex.

Marissa: please prepare the exec_approval_form.pdf with these conditions and route to me for signature. Jonas: let Procurement know we’re approved subject to the above, and coordinate the final SOW review with Legal.

Approved — Laura Bennett
